title: To the People worried about the opinions of AI haters
author: forgetscode
selftext:
Don't worry about them and focus on producing quality. The main issue with AI work is the flood of low effeort AI work that is slop. That's not AI though, that's a person posting something that's low effort. People were doing that before too but there wasn't as much.

Using AI has no bearing on the work you're making, it's still up to you to choose what stays at the end and make something quality. If someone's entire identity is dedicated to dismissing that and being a hater they aren't a person whose opinion should matter to you, that's the type of person who doesn't acheive anything worthwhile or else they don't have the time to go around and hate, they're doing something cool instead. 

The person who says your work was bad because it was low quality because of specifics, that's worth listening to and it's a shame that it's hard to get that now.

At the end of the day AI has made it cheaper to access quality work and that access is going to start reflecting in production later. 

A capitilist society means cheaper, higher quality, is eventually going to result in higher demand. It's a structural fact about the time it takes to produce quality assets with AI. A talented person is going to be able to produce quality with AI. In my opinion the disconnect is even with AI, quality work is not as easy as people make it out to be and no one is happy about the slop they're seeing.

So seperate those opinions from your process. Things got easier to make, it didn't actually make things easy. 

Every large technological advancement has gone through a similar amount of scrutinty, this time for better reason because these products are made to look good, without actually being good. That should inspire you to build something different from slop.

The printer, photography, recorded music, computer effects, digital art, If those things didn't get so much scrutiny they would have been low quality too. I don't hear anyone in the year 2026 still whining about their usage.

Build something that is actually good, that's what it has always been about. I think a lot of people are building something good right now.

comments.author: Annual-Kiwi4096
comments.body:
Theoretically you are right. Practically, a small organized group can harm your game.

They reduce the organic channels visibility by downvoting reddit posts, they actively attack content creators who are afraid of working with you and review bomb new games, which can be fatal to small creators.

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: If you're somehow getting enough attention from Antis that content creators are suddenly aware of your existence, those Antis are probably doing more to advertise your game than you could ever hope to do yourself.

replies.author: Annual-Kiwi4096
replies.body: Well that depends on how it goes. Suppose that a youtuber posts about your game a hate clip, yes you could get useful traffic. But what if you send to him a request to promote your game, and he says 'it looks great, but im afraid of my own audience, theyll harm my channel' ?

replies.author: forgetscode
replies.body:
do you know anyone who produced quality work that was affected like that?

if that happens and the work is truly quality, people like us should try to help them.

replies.author: Annual-Kiwi4096
replies.body:
Yes, I don't remember the name of the game, but he had a YouTube video where he described how he worked almost a year on tower defence game with excellent quality, with ai generated assets. 
At steam launch, anti ai haters targeted him, bought his game, put negative rating and refunded.
This reduced the velocity of his sales and harmed him significantly.
I'll find it in my history

replies.author: Odd-Complex8103
replies.body: Not tower defense, but similar story - [https://www.youtube.com/@randyprime](https://www.youtube.com/@randyprime)

replies.author: AmandasGameAccount
replies.body:
What’s crazy is games that don’t use AI at all can be harmed in the same way. All it takes is one person saying “just so you know this game uses AI” and suddenly a thread that loved it hates it now

But if you pay attention, the upvotes of the thread will still be in the +1650 but there’s 30 comments giving you toxic hate with anyone defending the game downvoted to -19. This math is actually a net positive to public opinion and more proof that the general public don’t care

comments.author: M4xs0n
comments.body: Yes, I actually found out a very successful game in the recent months made over 1 Million and used AI for some tiny stuff. AI disclosure on steam page, hate and boycott against it on reddit and even in official Steam discussions, the whole package. AND IT STILL was successful, because it was a good Game with an interesting concept. This was the final thing I needed to not give a Shit about Anti-AI comments etc. Its just not worth mentioning

replies.author: Steven_Broyles
replies.body: I too would like to know this game that made over 1 million after being brigaded- sounds made up imo

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: Not made up, but I had to correct myself. He sold 1 Million copies. But I guess at this point that detail isn’t that important

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: Librarian Tidy Up the Arcane Library. The developer announced in June that it had sold over 1 million copies. It had a generative AI disclosure on its Steam page before release, and there were already people calling for boycotts / saying they would not buy it because of AI before the game even launched. Still became a massive hit.

comments.author: arjuna66671
comments.body:
I see it with DLSS 5 - so many gamers changing their opinion because at the end of the day, they want a good looking game. Even more impressive are AI Star Wars fan film youtube channels. Some of them are so good and high quality that there isn't a single negative comment calling it slop that I can find. And we're talking about 500k+ views on a single video.

It's impossible not to see the artistic vision and skill in those works - even for sceptics.

Most of it is performative anyways and as always it will die down and in 2 years from now no one will care anymore.

replies.author: unfamily_friendly
replies.body: Kinda related. I noticed under AI music channels something like "Yes, this is AI, and i like it because of nostalgia etc". Many "good" comments under AI music are bots. But sometimes, i see the good comments, that doesn't look like bot posting at all. Some examples are written in Russian or Spanish (unpopular languages), with a grammar of drunk alcoholic, and completely on topic. Audience of AI consuming humans exists and it gives a hope

comments.author: InsolentCoolRadio
comments.body: “Win through your actions, never through argument.” -Robert Greene

comments.author: Odd-Complex8103
comments.body:
Over time it will likely become increasingly more mainstream and normalized, that's likely accurate.

I don't really agree on the no bearing part, there is a feeling of AI vs not in a game, but if the game is fun, then it's fun. 

I don't think the push should be there is no difference between the 2, there clearly is, but more that if a game is fun, then it's not less fun because it used AI in making it.

comments.author: Mammoth-Ad5262
comments.body:
Back in 2014 when I was in my degree for game design, I got introduced to Unity and already saw tons of Unity slop especially mediocre jumpscare games. Then UE4 went free and we got even more. Same thing happened with mobile games.

Thats just what happens when technology makes building stuff easier. Even without AI eventually some other technology wouldve made creation this accessible anyway.
